::: {.callout-important}
## Scope

AffineDrift tracks the review status of its own scientific claims with a falsification/critique apparatus (see [Critiques and Responses](../critiques/index.html)). A handful of words from that internal process — **governed**, **qualified**, **provenance**, **protected**, and **fail-closed** — occasionally appear in reader-facing prose. This page gives their plain-language meaning on this site, so a reader who has not seen the review apparatus is not left guessing.
:::

## Governed

A claim or workflow is **governed** when it is tracked by the site's critique/adjudication process: it has an open review record, and its status can change as evidence comes in. In prose, read "governed" as *"tracked and subject to review"* rather than as a legal or organizational sense of the word.

## Qualified

A **qualified** result is one presented with its limits stated up front — the scope, sample, or assumptions under which it holds — rather than as an unconditional finding. Read "qualified" as *"stated with its limits attached"*, not as a credential (as in "a qualified expert").

## Provenance

**Provenance** records where a claim, dataset, model, or software snapshot came from — its source, version, and chain of custody — so a reader can verify it independently. Read "provenance" as *"origin and version history"*.

## Protected

A **protected** branch accepts changes only through reviewed pull requests whose required checks pass; nothing can be pushed to it directly or rewritten. A **protected** commit is one on such a branch — for example "protected main". Read "protected" as *"landed through the repository's required review and checks"*.

## Fail-Closed

A **fail-closed** check or control is one that blocks by default when it cannot confirm a condition, rather than silently letting the condition pass. Read "fail-closed" as *"blocks by default when unsure"*.
